sections.heading: How to check your pronunciation
sections.body:
Open the checker and choose the language you are practising. Then type a word or sentence, or pick one from the list. Press Hear it first if you want to hear the correct pronunciation, then press Say it and read the text aloud.

1. Open the [pronunciation checker](https://pronunciation-checker.lazur.app/).
2. Choose the language you are practising from the list.
3. Type a word or sentence, or pick one.
4. Press Say it. When the browser asks for the microphone, select Allow.
5. Read the text out loud at normal speed.
6. Look at the result. Each word is marked right or wrong.

Speak each word clearly, with a short pause between words. The engine can only judge what it hears, so a clean, even attempt gives a more useful result than a rushed one.

sections.heading: What the score and the marks mean
sections.body:
The score is the share of target words that the engine heard as correct, shown as a percentage. Each word in the text gets its own mark, so you can see exactly which words to practise. A perfect score means every word in the text was marked right.

**The marks show what the engine heard, not how a native speaker would hear you.** A word can be marked wrong even when your pronunciation is close, because the result is based on what the engine caught. Treat the marks as a guide to the words to repeat.

Press Hear it and compare the correct version with your own attempt. Repeat the same text until every word is marked right, then move on to a longer sentence. Doing the same text again on another day shows whether your practice is working.

sections.heading: If the checker cannot hear you
sections.body:
If the result does not appear, or the page says it cannot hear you, check the microphone first. Chrome needs permission for each site before it can use the mic.

1. Select Allow when the browser asks for the microphone. If you chose Never allow earlier, open Chrome's Settings, then Privacy and security, then Site settings, then Microphone, and change this site to allowed.
2. Check that you are not muted, including any mute switch on your headset.
3. Check that the microphone you want is the default recording device in your computer's sound settings.
4. Reload the page, then press Say it again.

Chrome's help page on the microphone is at [support.google.com/chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/2693767). If it still does not work, restart Chrome, then restart the computer and try again.

sections.heading: Your browser decides how the test runs
sections.body:
The checker uses the speech recognition built into your browser. The engine does the listening and judges each word, so the result depends on the language you chose, the microphone you use and the browser itself. Two different browsers can mark the same attempt differently.

A quiet room and a headset with a clear microphone usually give the most even results. If you are practising for a call or a class, use the same headset and the same spot you will use then. A different mic can change the marks for the same words, so keep your setup the same when you compare scores.

sections.heading: What a right or wrong mark tells you
sections.body:
Each word is marked against what the browser's speech engine heard. Right means the engine heard the word you were aiming for. Wrong means it heard something else, or it could not match your speech to that word. That is a useful signal, but it is not a verdict on your accent or your English as a whole.

**A wrong mark is a prompt to listen again, not proof of a mistake.** Hear the correct version, then say the word slowly at normal volume and try again. If the mark changes, your attempt was the difference. If it stays wrong after several tries, check the microphone and the language before you change how you say the word.

The score is the share of words marked right. It shows how your attempt compares with the text you chose. It does not show which sound in a word was off, so use Hear it to hear the difference yourself.

When every word is marked wrong, the cause is usually the setup, not the words. Check these in order.

2. Select Allow for the microphone in your browser. If you blocked it earlier, change the site to allowed in the browser's site settings.

4. Close any other app that might be using the mic, such as a call app or a recorder.

faq.q: Can I test German pronunciation online?
faq.a: Yes. Open the checker, choose German, allow the microphone when asked, and press Say it. Each word is marked right or wrong, and Hear it plays the correct version. Nothing is installed.
